'''Heinz Kaminski''' (15 June 1921 – 17 February 2002) was a German [[chemical engineering|chemical engineer]] and space researcher.

== Biography ==
Heinz Kaminski founded and later directed the  [[Bochum Observatory]]. He also busied himself with environmental research. Although Kaminski was only an amateur astronomer and not a professional, the press constantly treated him as a source of information on astronomical events. At the end of the 1970s and the beginning of the 1980s, Kaminski took an active interest in politics - at first in the [[:de:Grüne Aktion Zukunft|Green Party]], then in the [[:de:Die Bürgerpartei|Bürgerpartei]].

In the cellar of his house, Kaminski, a former naval radio operator, had built a receiving station from old wooden tables and in the meadow in front of his house in the Bochum district of Sundern erected an [[Antenna (radio)|antenna]] assisted by three co-workers, with whose help he listened in to radio signals from space. During the night of 7 October 1957, Kaminski receive signals from [[Sputnik 1]], the first artificial satellite in space.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1957 |title=ULB Bonn / 76 (1957) [1239 |url=http://zeitpunkt.nrw/ulbbn/4324096 |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=zeitpunkt.nrw |language=en}}</ref> Even he was not the first person outside the Soviet territories,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Course Recorded -- Navy Picks Up Radio Signals -- 4 Report Sighting Device |url=https://archive.nytimes.com/www.nytimes.com/partners/aol/special/sputnik/sput-02.html |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=archive.nytimes.com}}</ref> as an urban myth in Bochum tells, nor the first person in Germany,<ref>{{Cite web| title=Telescopium - Mitteilungen der Volkssternwarte Bonn, Astronomische Vereinigung e.V. | year=2007 | url=https://www.volkssternwarte-bonn.de/wordpress/wp-content/downloads/Telescopium0704.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210926131430/https://www.volkssternwarte-bonn.de/wordpress/wp-content/downloads/Telescopium0704.pdf | archive-date=2021-09-26}}</ref> he and Bochum becomes very popular about this fact.

In 1961, Kaminski took over the leadership of the {{lang|de|Volkssternwarte Bochum}} (Bochum People's Observatory), which had been founded by himself. During the years he built the grounds around the Volkssternwarte into an Institute and made sure that it managed a connection to international space research. At the Bochum Station, signals from a variety of space vehicles from the Sputniks, [[Luna programme|Lunik]]s up to [[Vostok programme|Vostok]] and [[Voskhod programme|Voskhod]] could be received, as well as in 1963 (for the first time in Europe) satellite pictures from the US weather satellite [[TIROS]]-8. In 1967 Kaminski installed a {{convert|20|m|adj=on}} parabolic antenna in a [[radome]], with which all [[Apollo program|Apollo mission]]s were followed. When his Institut was denied subsidies in 1982, Kaminski changed the Volkssternwarte Bochum into the private "Institut für Umwelt- und Zukunftsforschung" (IUZ) (Institute for Environmental and Future Research), which over the years has developed into a top-rate educational institution.

Due to the efforts of Kaminski, the city of Bochum erected in 1964 the first post-war large planetarium in Deutschland (equipped at the time with a Zeiss Mod. IV). Kaminski was nominated as the first direktor and occupied this position until his retirement in 1986.

In 1972 Kaminski became an honorary professor in the [[Physics]] Department at the [[University of Essen]] and gave lectures until the Winter semester 1999/2000 on "Environmental Research via Satellite - Results and Political Consequences".

On 17 February 2002, Kaminski died at the age of 80. He had three children.
